notes: Fluorescence flow cytometry (not mass cytometry) whole-blood myeloid panel from a COVID-19 cohort. Steps 1–5 are acquisition / scatter / live cleanup; Step 6 splits PMN from mononuclear; Steps 7–24 walk the granulocyte, lymphocyte, monocyte, DC, and basophil branches. Single-category labeling convention: most steps annotate only the positively-called population (e.g. `Live`, `Cells`, `Singlets1`) and leave the remainder unannotated, because the remainder is not a defined cell type. The `x_marker` / `y_marker` fields use raw fluorophore channel names (`Comp-XXX-A`); the channel→protein mapping is in `parquet/meta.json` (e.g. Comp-PE-A = CD86, Comp-BV421-A = CD14, Comp-APC-Cy7-A = L/D).

steps.note: Time stability gate — retain only events within a stable acquisition window. The Time x-axis is the primary discriminator (excludes drift / fluid-disturbance regions at the start or end of the run, e.g. clogs, air bubbles, sample-end artifacts). The y-axis (Comp-APC-A, CD1c) serves two additional functions beyond pure display: (1) channel-stability QC — a fluorescence channel is plotted against time so that any time-localized drift or shift in fluorescence intensity (laser warmup, cytometer instability, sample evaporation) becomes visible and the affected time window can be excluded; (2) vertical outlier exclusion — events that spike abnormally high on the y-axis (electronic noise, abnormal events) within an otherwise stable time window can be removed by drawing a polygon rather than a strict 1D cutoff on Time. Time_stable: events inside the stable Time × fluorescence polygon. Any bright/stable fluorescence channel could serve the y-axis role; CD1c is used here for convenience.

Forward/side scatter cleanup to isolate intact white blood cells. Cells: events within a broad WBC scatter envelope that includes the lymphocyte (FSC-low / SSC-low), monocyte (FSC-mid / SSC-mid), and granulocyte (FSC-mid-to-high / SSC-high) clusters as a single polygon. Excluded: lower-left debris (FSC-low / SSC-low events smaller than lymphocytes — RBC fragments, platelets, dead-cell remnants, free fluorochrome / dye aggregates near the SSC baseline) and upper-right aggregates (FSC very high / SSC very high — cell clumps and large doublets that pre-empt the dedicated singlet gates at Steps 3–4). The three WBC clusters often touch one another on the FSC × SSC plane, so the gate is drawn as one inclusive envelope rather than separate per-population polygons.

First singlet discrimination on the SSC-H × SSC-A diagonal — singlet events fall on the linear diagonal; doublets/aggregates deviate because area scales faster than height when two events are coincident.

Second singlet discrimination on SSC-W × SSC-A — SSC-W (pulse width) flags residual doublets that passed the H-vs-A gate; true singlets have a narrow, stereotyped pulse width while doublets show inflated width.

Nominal viability gate. In this dataset's expert-curated workspace, the gate at this step does not enforce a strict L/D-based exclusion — effectively all events passing Step 4 are labeled Live. The L/D channel (Comp-APC-Cy7-A, y) and CD86 channel (Comp-PE-A, x) are retained on the plot for visual QC of staining quality and dead-cell distribution, but they are not used to drop events. Possible reasons (not confirmed in the workspace): whole-blood RBC-lysis preparations typically have very low dead-cell fractions, and/or downstream analysis was judged not to be sensitive to residual L/D-positive contamination. Live: all events from Step 4 (Singlets2). Note for downstream interpretation: any L/D-positive contamination is carried into all subsequent populations, so dim/non-specific signal in fluorescence channels of downstream subsets may include a small dead-cell contribution.

Split polymorphonuclear (granulocytes) from mononuclear leukocytes. PMN: SSC-high and CD14-negative (granulocytes have large granular cytoplasm → high SSC, and are CD14-low). Non_PMN: SSC-lower (lymphocytes, monocytes, DCs; includes CD14+ monocytes which are resolved downstream). In-panel co-marker prior: there is no positive granulocyte lineage marker in this panel, so PMN is defined by scatter morphology plus CD14-negativity; the remaining in-panel markers (CD3, CD19, HLA-DR, CD11c, CD1c, CD303, CD123, CD86, CD16) do not add discriminative power at this split — CD16 is reserved for the downstream neutrophil / eosinophil separation at Step 7.

Granulocyte subsetting within PMN. Neutrophils: CD16+ (FcγRIII-high; mature neutrophils). Eosinophils: CD16- (eosinophils are classically CD16-negative/low). In-panel co-marker prior: no in-panel marker positively confirms eosinophil identity — CD16 negativity within the high-SSC PMN parent is the sole discriminator, so eosinophils here are defined by exclusion. Basophils (CD16- CD123+) are captured via a separate branch at Step 24, not here, and should not contaminate the PMN parent because basophils have lower SSC than granulocytes; CD123 is therefore not needed at this step.

Lymphocyte lineage split within mononuclear cells. B_Cells: CD19+ CD3- (mature B-lineage). T_Cells: CD3+ CD19- (T-lineage). Non_BT: CD19- CD3- (feeds the myeloid / DC / basophil branches — monocytes, DCs, NK cells, basophils, and any residual CD3-CD19- lineages). Note: NK cells are not resolved in this panel (no CD56 / CD16-based NK gate on the lymphoid branch); they end up within Non_BT. In-panel co-marker prior: none of the other in-panel markers (CD14, CD16, HLA-DR, CD11c, CD123, CD303, CD1c, CD86) are lineage-discriminative for B vs. T — CD3/CD19 are the only lymphoid lineage markers in this panel, so B_Cells and T_Cells are each defined by a single positive call without an in-panel confirmatory co-marker.

B-cell activation readout. B_cells_CD86p: CD86+ (activated B cells; CD86 is up-regulated on antigen-engaged B cells as a T-cell co-stimulatory ligand). Axis design caveat: y_marker is CD3, but parent is already CD3- by the B_Cells gate at Step 8 — CD3 on y is a purity sanity-check axis (events should cluster at CD3-low); the activation call is driven by CD86 on x. In-panel co-marker prior: HLA-DR (Comp-BV510-A) is constitutively high on B cells and is further up-regulated on activated B cells — it can serve as a complementary activation/APC-licensing readout alongside CD86 if needed, although it is not used for the gate call here.

Canonical three-way monocyte subsetting on CD14 × CD16. Classical_monocytes: CD14++ CD16- (most abundant, inflammatory, main pool of blood monocytes). Intermediate_monocytes: CD14++ CD16+ (transitional, expanded in inflammation). Patrolling_monocytes: CD14+ CD16++ (non-classical / patrolling, vasculature-surveillance). Non_monocytes: CD14-low (feeds the DC branch at Steps 14–22). Useful co-markers: HLA-DR confirms monocyte identity (all monocyte subsets are HLA-DR+) and is used downstream at Step 14 to enrich the DC branch within Non_monocytes.

Activation readout for classical monocytes. CM_CD86p: CD86+ activated classical monocytes (CD86 up-regulation marks antigen-presenting capacity / pro-inflammatory state). Naming caveat: the prefix `CM` here stands for 'Classical Monocyte' — not to be confused with 'Central Memory' used in T-cell panels of other cohorts. In-panel co-marker prior: HLA-DR (Comp-BV510-A) is expressed on all monocytes and is typically further up-regulated with CD86 on activated / inflammatory monocytes — it can serve as an in-panel complementary activation readout.

Activation readout for intermediate monocytes. IM_CD86p: CD86+ activated intermediate monocytes. The intermediate subset is the most pro-inflammatory compartment in many disease states (including COVID-19), so CD86 up-regulation here is a key disease-activity readout. In-panel co-marker prior: HLA-DR (Comp-BV510-A) is characteristically highest on intermediate monocytes among the three subsets at baseline and tends to co-move with CD86 on inflammatory activation — useful as an in-panel complementary activation readout, and its shift can be cross-checked against CD86 to detect monocyte dysregulation (HLA-DR-low with CD86-normal has been reported in severe COVID-19).

Activation readout for patrolling (non-classical) monocytes. PM_CD86p: CD86+ activated patrolling monocytes. Patrolling monocytes are normally less APC-competent than classical monocytes; CD86 up-regulation indicates a licensed / inflammatory state. In-panel co-marker prior: HLA-DR (Comp-BV510-A) is expressed on patrolling monocytes and tends to co-move with CD86 on activation — useful as an in-panel complementary activation readout.

Enrich HLA-DR+ antigen-presenting cells within the Non_monocytes fraction — the entry point to the DC branch. HLADRp: HLA-DR+ (dendritic cells are uniformly HLA-DR-high; remaining HLA-DR- events in this parent include residual NK cells, basophils with low HLA-DR, or other lineages that are routed out here). In-panel co-marker prior: DC identity is confirmed downstream using in-panel markers — CD11c+ (Comp-BV650-A, Step 18) for mDCs and CD303+/CD123+ (Comp-FITC-A / Comp-PerCP-Cy5-5-A, Step 16) for pDCs — so HLA-DR positivity alone is not a DC call, it is only the DC-candidate enrichment step. The HLA-DR- events dropped here are correctly routed out of the DC branch and are separately captured by the Step 23 basophil-candidate branch (HLADRn_CD14n) off the same Non_BT parent.

Remove residual CD16+ contaminants from the DC candidate pool. HLADRp_CD16n: CD16- (classical DC populations are CD16-low; CD16+ events at this stage are typically residual CD16+ monocytes that spilled through the Non_monocytes gate, or CD16+ NK-like cells with HLA-DR expression — both excluded here). The remaining CD16-negative, HLA-DR-positive events feed the pDC / mDC split at Step 16. In-panel co-marker prior: the y_marker CD14 (Comp-BV421-A) is shown as a display/purity axis — the Non_monocytes parent from Step 10 has already enforced CD14-low, so events should cluster at CD14-low; visible CD14+ residuals here indicate monocyte spillover through Step 10 and help diagnose upstream gate quality, but CD14 is not used for the call.

Plasmacytoid vs. non-plasmacytoid DC split. pDC: CD303+ CD123+ (plasmacytoid DCs; CD303/BDCA-2 is the lineage-specific marker, CD123/IL-3Rα confirms; this double-positive combination is the canonical pDC identity). Non_pDC: CD303- CD123- (proceeds to the myeloid DC branch at Step 18). In-panel co-marker prior: CD123 alone is not pDC-specific within PBMC — basophils are also CD123+ — so the CD303 axis is essential for the positive call. In this gating tree basophils are already excluded upstream by the HLA-DR+ parent gate (Step 14) since basophils are HLA-DR- and are instead captured by the Step 23 branch; this means CD123+ events reaching Step 16 should almost entirely be pDCs, and the CD303 requirement serves as a cross-confirmation rather than a strict baso-discriminator.

Activation readout for pDCs. pDC_CD86p: CD86+ activated pDCs. pDCs are the major type-I IFN producers in antiviral responses; CD86 up-regulation marks their co-stimulatory licensing state, particularly relevant in viral infections like COVID-19. In-panel co-marker prior: HLA-DR (Comp-BV510-A) is constitutively high on pDCs (already enforced by the Step 14 parent) and is further up-regulated on maturation — useful as an in-panel complementary licensing readout alongside CD86.

Positive selection of myeloid DCs within the Non_pDC compartment. mDC: CD11c+ (integrin αX; pan-myeloid DC marker; conventional DCs are CD11c-high). The remaining CD11c- events are not annotated at this step (not a defined cell type in this panel). In-panel co-marker prior: HLA-DR (Comp-BV510-A, from the Step 14 parent) is uniformly high on mDCs — events calling mDC here should cluster at HLA-DR-high; HLA-DR-dim CD11c+ events would be atypical and suggest residual NK-like contamination. The CD1c subsetting at Step 19 then provides in-panel lineage refinement within mDC.

Myeloid DC subsetting by CD1c (BDCA-1). As labeled in this file: mDC1 = CD1c+, mDC2 = CD1c-. Nomenclature caveat: in the canonical cDC1 / cDC2 convention, cDC1 = CD141+ (BDCA-3+) cross-presenting DCs and cDC2 = CD1c+ (BDCA-1+) inflammatory DCs — so the CD1c+ subset is conventionally cDC2, not cDC1. The label mapping in this panel (CD1c+ → mDC1) therefore appears to be inverted relative to the canonical convention; whether this is intentional (lab-specific naming) or an error should be verified with the panel author. CD141 is not in this panel, so a true cDC1 gate cannot be established — the CD1c- events here are an unlabeled residual rather than confirmed cDC1.

Aggregate activation readout for all mDCs (both subtypes combined). mDC_CD86p: CD86+ activated mDCs. Complementary to the subtype-specific activation gates at Steps 21 and 22. In-panel co-marker prior: HLA-DR (Comp-BV510-A, from the Step 14 parent) is up-regulated on mDC maturation alongside CD86 and serves as an in-panel complementary licensing readout.

Activation readout for the mDC1 subset (CD1c+ as labeled in this panel). mDC1_CD86p: CD86+ activated mDC1. Subject to the Step 19 nomenclature caveat above. In-panel co-marker prior: HLA-DR (Comp-BV510-A, from the Step 14 parent) is a complementary maturation readout that tends to co-move with CD86 on DCs.

Activation readout for the mDC2 subset (CD1c- as labeled in this panel). mDC2_CD86p: CD86+ activated mDC2. Subject to the Step 19 nomenclature caveat above. In-panel co-marker prior: HLA-DR (Comp-BV510-A, from the Step 14 parent) is a complementary maturation readout that tends to co-move with CD86 on DCs.

Parallel branch off Non_BT (sibling to the monocyte/DC branch starting at Step 10) — enrich the HLA-DR-negative, CD14-negative compartment to isolate basophil candidates. HLADRn_CD14n: HLA-DR- CD14- (basophils are HLA-DR- and CD14-; this gate removes monocytes and DCs, but most NK cells are HLA-DR- CD14- and therefore remain in this parent alongside basophils). In-panel co-marker prior: the residual NK-cell contamination in HLADRn_CD14n is filtered at Step 24 by CD123+ selection (basophils are CD123+ while NK cells are CD123-), so this step is deliberately broad — specificity comes from CD123 downstream, not from HLA-DR / CD14 here.

Positive identification of basophils within the HLA-DR- CD14- compartment. Basophils: CD123+ (IL-3Rα-high; combined with HLA-DR- and CD14- enforced by upstream parents, this is a canonical basophil signature). In-panel co-marker prior: CD16 is displayed on the x-axis as a negative purity check — basophils are CD16-, so events calling Basophils should cluster at CD16-low; visible CD16+ residuals here would suggest NK-cell contamination that escaped Step 23 and should be excluded. The positive call is driven by CD123 on y. The HLA-DR- and CD14- parent state (Step 23) together with CD123+ here are the only in-panel discriminators — no more specific basophil marker is present in this panel.
